time_plan.30m: Check whether the market probability move is sustained or a thin-liquidity blip; cross-check with 2y/10y yields and fed funds futures (SOFR) for confirmation.
time_plan.1h: Compare TLT move to SHY/IEF (front/belly) — if curve is bull-steepening via front end, confirms dovish rate-path read.
time_plan.2h: Look for any macro catalyst (CPI, jobs, Fed speak) that may already be public and driving both the market and bonds.
time_plan.6h: Re-assess whether yields holding lower or mean-reverting; check dollar and gold for corroboration of a dovish regime.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate net TLT move vs expectation; note if signal faded, indicating noise rather than genuine information leakage.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of six 25bp Fed cuts in 2026 reflects a dovish repricing of the policy path (weaker growth/inflation or recession fears). That lowers the expected path of the fed funds rate, pulling Treasury yields down and bond prices up. TLT is the most rate-sensitive liquid proxy, so a dovish shift should lift it. The effect on the long end is muted vs the front end because six cuts is mostly a front/belly story and long yields also embed growth/term-premium dynamics.

predictions.reasoning: More expected Fed cuts narrows US rate differentials versus other economies, typically a headwind for the dollar. A sharp rise in six-cut odds would therefore tend to weaken the broad dollar, with UUP a liquid proxy. The move is small and noisy because FX also depends on relative central-bank stances abroad; if the dovish shift reflects global risk-off, the dollar could instead strengthen as a haven, which caps confidence.

evidence_used: Market question implies probability of six 25bp Fed cuts in 2026, a strongly dovish policy-path scenario
Standard macro linkage: more expected cuts => lower expected fed funds path => lower yields, weaker dollar, supportive for gold
Liquid rate/FX proxies (TLT, UUP) respond to shifts in expected Fed policy
uncertainty_notes: The 700bps tradability threshold is far above realistic 12h moves for these liquid proxies, so neither prediction is tradable by that bar
Direction of the market move (rising vs falling six-cut odds) is not specified; thesis assumes a sharp INCREASE in dovish odds
Dovish repricing driven by recession fears could trigger risk-off that strengthens the dollar, reversing the FX call
Topic tag 'military_conflict' seems mislabeled; treated as a pure Fed-policy market

llm_justification.summary: This is a US monetary-policy market: a jump in the odds of six 2026 rate cuts signals a dovish repricing of the Fed path. The cleanest liquid implications are lower Treasury yields (TLT up) and a softer dollar (UUP down). Both effects are modest and noisy over a 12h window — well below the 700bps tradable threshold — and could reverse if the dovish signal reflects recession/risk-off dynamics that bid the dollar as a haven. Confidence is low; this is a weak, noisy mapping rather than a clean signal.
key_assumptions: The anomaly is a sharp INCREASE in the implied probability of six cuts (more dovish)
The move reflects genuine policy-path information, not thin-market noise
No offsetting global central-bank or risk-off dynamics dominate
Standard rate-differential and duration channels hold
failure_modes: The dovish shift stems from recession fear, causing risk-off that strengthens USD and muddies TLT (credit/term-premium effects)
Information is already public (e.g., post-CPI/jobs/Fed-speak), so assets already priced it and no leakage edge exists
Proxies are weakly exposed: six cuts is a front-end story while TLT is long-end; UUP depends heavily on foreign central banks
The prediction-market move reverses as a liquidity blip, with no corresponding asset move
Moves are an order of magnitude below the 700bps tradability bar, so signal is non-actionable even if directionally right
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
